key_insight: Adaptive finite elements achieve linear convergence and optimal algebraic rates in W^{1,p} for the Dirichlet Poisson problem under continuous well-posedness and discrete inf-sup stability.
engineering_relevance: The analysis supports reliable adaptive meshing in W^{1,p} norms on potentially nonconvex domains, with relevance to Poisson-type engineering models.
method: Keep Galerkin equations unchanged; adapt residual estimation and Dörfler marking to exponent p.
Extend relaxed quasi-orthogonality to Banach spaces using discrete inf-sup stability.
Use sufficiently small marking fractions and nearly minimal marked sets for rate optimality.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence and optimality proofs, verifies the stability hypotheses for p sufficiently close to 2, and provides no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: Beyond p sufficiently close to 2, continuous well-posedness and discrete inf-sup stability must be established separately.
paper_title: Optimal adaptive finite element methods in $W^{1,p}$
